assignment.review_focus: Risk document version alignment in verification records. Risk Traceability Agent (RUN-0003) and V&V Agent (RUN-0007) both flagged that the design verification plan/report cites PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0 while the active risk management report is V2.0. This recheck must: (1) retrieve the design verification plan/report and identify every location where PT9L-FXGB01 is cited, recording the version number cited at each location; (2) retrieve PT9L-FXGB01 V2.0 and identify what changed between V1.0 and V2.0 — specifically whether any risk controls added or modified in V2.0 have corresponding verification activities in the verification plan/report; (3) determine whether any change record, amendment, or addendum to the verification plan/report acknowledges the V2.0 update; (4) assess whether the closed-loop confirmation between risk controls and verification activities is broken by this version mismatch. Do not render a finding verdict — locate and report all available evidence.

assignment.review_focus: Risk document version alignment in verification records. Risk Traceability Agent (RUN-0003) and V&V Agent (RUN-0007) both flagged that the design verification plan/report cites PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0 while the active risk management report is V2.0. This recheck must: (1) retrieve the design verification plan/report and identify every location where PT9L-FXGB01 is cited, recording the version number cited at each location; (2) retrieve PT9L-FXGB01 V2.0 and identify what changed between V1.0 and V2.0 — specifically whether any risk controls added or modified in V2.0 have corresponding verification activities in the verification plan/report; (3) determine whether any change record, amendment, or addendum to the verification plan/report acknowledges the V2.0 update; (4) assess whether the closed-loop confirmation between risk controls and verification activities is broken by this version mismatch. Do not render a finding verdict — locate and report all available evidence.

agent_runs.summary: Cross-corpus scan of the PT9L DHF/DMR package reveals 14 candidate consistency issues spanning legacy product residue in active documents, document-number mismatches, unsigned approvals, wrong-product references in BOM and label documents, regulatory applicability conflicts, software diagram contamination, and blood-pressure-specific language appearing in a thermometer DHF.

Hardware audit of PT9L DHF/DMR reveals five substantive consistency findings: a blood-pressure residue phrase in the battery design-verification plan/report, an unresolved BOM conflict between PT3-P10 dual-spring and PT5-M02/M03 separate springs, a total-assembly drawing part-number anomaly (T-Z1-P10 used for two distinct PCBs), missing pass/fail verdicts in multiple T1 sample review checklists, and object-temperature mode accuracy tolerance (±0.2 °C) applied at 30 °C and 45 °C in software test plans despite the design-input accuracy specification only requiring ±0.2 °C for ≥35 °C and ≤42 °C.

The PT9L risk management file set contains multiple traceability chain breaks: the current Risk Management Report references document number PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0 while the active risk set has been revised to V2.0; the active Risk Management Plan carries document number IFT-FXJH01 rather than PT9L-FXJH01; F0013 (PT2L risk plan) internally carries a PT9L-series document number creating a product-identity conflict; no evidence of Bluetooth-specific hazard verification is present in the supplied corpus; DFMEA files (F0071, F0074) are not cross-referenced to the ISO 14971 risk assessment; and the design verification plan/report cites only PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0 while the current report is V2.0, leaving the closed-loop confirmation potentially misaligned.

PT9L software lifecycle audit reveals five substantive findings: BP3L software diagrams appear in the primary PT9L software design folder and T1 sample subfolder without documented shared-component rationale; the software design document version identifier (E0 23.11) cannot be reconciled with the V1.0 identifier cited in test/validation records and BOM; no Bluetooth software requirements or corresponding test/validation evidence is present in the supplied corpus; the IEC 60601-1 test report references software design document DN:PT9L-RJFA01 V1.0 which does not appear in the evidence catalog; and a label review document filed under the active T1 sample folder carries PT2L as the primary product model without justification.

DMR/SOP audit of PT9L design output chain reveals seven substantive findings including a document-number collision on drawing PT9L-F01, a part-number mismatch between the two packaging BOM files, PT3-origin shared-component drawings archived in the PT9L DHF without cross-product justification, an incomplete drawing title-block in a packaging label drawing, a missing outer-carton BOM entry in the primary packaging BOM, a process instruction referencing EBOM by document number without pinning a version, and the design output list carrying blank approval-date fields indicating the formal sign-off record is incomplete.

PT9L DHF regulatory audit identifies eight substantive findings spanning unsigned approval fields across all risk management documents, dual ASTM E1965 version citation without documented transition rationale, inconsistent EN ISO 80601-2-56 and MDR 2017/745 applicability between design input stages, absent 510(k) responsibility agreement for 'andon', biocompatibility reports conducted on PT5 samples rather than PT9L, IFT-prefixed document numbers on active PT9L risk management plans, a historical-folder risk plan (F0013) carrying a PT9L-series document number, and the operation guide referencing MDD rather than MDR for biocompatibility compliance.

PT9L V&V corpus audit reveals five substantive findings: object-temperature accuracy tolerance applied outside the design-input specified range without documented justification; no Bluetooth hazard or functional verification evidence present; blood-pressure residue phrase in battery verification record with no confirmed signed pass verdict in supplied evidence; no verification record references the controlling risk document at V2.0; and the IEC 60601-1 test report's cited software design document (PT9L-RJFA01 V1.0) is absent from the evidence catalog and design output index.

Cross-run synthesis audit of the PT9L DHF/DMR package identifies six substantive regulatory and document-control findings, including one systemic finding covering unsigned approvals across all risk management documents, plus resolution assessments on five specific escalation questions raised by the orchestrator.

Full-corpus recheck for Bluetooth hazard traceability in the PT9L risk management chain confirms a true gap: no evidence of Bluetooth/BLE/wireless/RF hazard identification, risk control, or verification closure exists in any supplied document, while the project profile explicitly states PT9L transmits temperature via Bluetooth, and the active Risk Management Report (PT9L-FXGB01 V2.0, F0020/F0024) contains no retrievable Bluetooth hazard entry in the supplied evidence.

llm_output.summary: Context recheck for ASG-0010 confirms that the design verification report (F0114) cites external test reports ETX202303-07-078-03 and ETX202303-07-078-04 as passing evidence for ISO 80601-2-56 and ASTM E1965 compliance, but no version of the verification plan/report in the supplied evidence catalog explicitly cites PT9L-FXGB01 by version number, no change record or addendum acknowledging the V1.0-to-V2.0 risk report update is present, a revised ISO 80601-2-56 test report (ETX202303-07-078-03R1, dated 2025-05-29) exists in the corpus without any corresponding update to the design verification report, and the closed-loop confirmation between risk controls and verification activities cannot be confirmed as complete from the supplied evidence.
review_notes: The design verification report (F0114) is a multi-row matrix document covering regulatory standards; the supplied evidence lines (VV-010 through VV-015) represent only the rows for ISO 80601-2-56:2017/Amd1:2018, EN ISO 80601-2-56:2017+A1:2018, EN 12470-3, EN 12470-5, ASTM E1965-98:2016, and ASTM E1965-98:2023. No other rows from F0114 are present in the evidence catalog, so a complete audit of all verification plan rows is not possible from supplied evidence alone.

The risk management report exists in two document instances: F0020 (doc_id F0020, path '03 风险分析\Attachment 7 04 Risk Management Report IFT-FXGB01 V2.0') and F0024 (doc_id F0024, path '03 风险分析\PT9L--Attachment 7 04 Risk Management Report IFT-FXGB01 V2.0'). Both carry V2.0 in their filenames. The supplied evidence lines for both (VV-001 through VV-004) contain only high-level statements about the risk management plan and acceptance criteria; no line-level content showing what changed between V1.0 and V2.0 is present in the evidence catalog.

Five final external test reports are present in the corpus: ETX202303-07-078-01 (EMC, F0456), ETX202303-07-078-02 (safety/IEC 60601-1, F0457), ETX202303-07-078-03 (ISO 80601-2-56, F0458), ETX202303-07-078-04 (ASTM E1965, F0459), ETX202303-07-078-05 (aging/老化, F0460). All are dated 2025-02-12 except the EMC report (2024-08-15).

A revised ISO 80601-2-56 report ETX202303-07-078-03R1 (F0461, dated 2025-05-29) is present in the corpus. This is a later revision of the same test scope as ETX202303-07-078-03. The design verification report (F0114) cites only ETX202303-07-078-03 and ETX202303-07-078-04 for ISO 80601-2-56 compliance; it does not reference the R1 revision.

Draft versions of reports ETX202303-07-078-01 (F0465), ETX202303-07-078-02 (F0466), ETX202303-07-078-03 (F0467), and ETX202303-07-078-04 (F0468) are present in the '草稿' (draft) subfolder. The draft for ETX202303-07-078-02 (F0466) carries a truncated report number 'ETX2023-07-078-02' (missing '03' segment) in its header lines, which differs from the final report number 'ETX202303-07-078-02'.

The usability engineering file (F0247/F0248) describes acceptance criteria for usability evaluation and references two formative evaluations and a summative/pre-summative evaluation, but no summative usability test report or completed formative evaluation report is present in the supplied evidence catalog.

The design input summary table (F0031/F0319) is present in the evidence catalog only as a title line ('Design Input - General part') with no retrievable content rows, so traceability from specific design inputs to verification activities cannot be confirmed from supplied evidence.
The DFMEA files (F0071, F0074) reference pass/fail acceptance criteria in their detection rating scales but are not cross-referenced to any specific verification test record in the supplied evidence.

No document identified as the verification plan (PT9L-KXPS01) appears in the evidence catalog by that document number; F0114 is the only verification-related document with retrievable content rows, and it is labeled as a design verification report rather than a plan.

The analysis and evaluation report (F0462) references 'Annex I: ETX202303-07-078-05 Test Report' as an annex, and two copies of that annex exist in the corpus (F0455 in '实验报告' root and F0463 in '实验报告\最终报告'). Both carry the same report number ETX202303-07-078-05. The final aging report (F0460) also carries ETX202303-07-078-05. The relationship between the annex copies and the standalone final report is not clarified in the supplied evidence.

findings.claim: The design verification report (F0114) cites external test reports ETX202303-07-078-03 and ETX202303-07-078-04 as the sole evidence of ISO 80601-2-56 and ASTM E1965 compliance, but a revised report ETX202303-07-078-03R1 (dated 2025-05-29) exists in the corpus and is not referenced in F0114, leaving the verification record potentially superseded without documented acknowledgment.
findings.rationale: VV-010 and VV-014/VV-015 show F0114 citing ETX202303-07-078-03 and ETX202303-07-078-04 as passing evidence for ISO 80601-2-56:2017/Amd1:2018 and ASTM E1965-98:2016/2023 respectively. VV-067 through VV-070 confirm that ETX202303-07-078-03R1 (F0461) is a formal report dated 2025-05-29, which post-dates the original ETX202303-07-078-03 (F0458, dated 2025-02-12). The existence of an R1 revision implies the original report was superseded or supplemented. No evidence in the catalog shows F0114 being updated to reference ETX202303-07-078-03R1, and no change record or addendum to F0114 is present in the supplied evidence. If ETX202303-07-078-03R1 was issued to correct a test failure or scope gap, the verification closure recorded in F0114 may be based on a superseded report.
challenge_questions: What was the reason for issuing ETX202303-07-078-03R1 on 2025-05-29? Was it issued to correct a test failure, address a scope gap, or for administrative reasons?
Has F0114 (design verification report) been updated to reference ETX202303-07-078-03R1 as the controlling test report for ISO 80601-2-56 compliance? If so, where is that updated version?
Does ETX202303-07-078-03R1 supersede ETX202303-07-078-03, or are both reports valid and complementary? Is there a supersession statement in either report?
If ETX202303-07-078-03R1 contains different test results or conclusions from ETX202303-07-078-03, what is the impact on the design verification closure recorded in F0114?
